react_result.final_narrative_text: Cross-paradigm pathway analysis of the 10 input metabolites reveals a compelling convergence on tyrosine metabolism. The RAMP multi-database ORA identified KEGG:map00350 "Tyrosine metabolism" at rank 7 (FDR = 1.39e-09) with a fold enrichment of 522, driven by four metabolites: L-tyrosine, norepinephrine, fumaric acid, and 3,4-dihydroxyphenylacetaldehyde. This finding was independently replicated by MetaboAnalystR PSEA, which ranked KEGG:hsa00350 (the human namespace equivalent) as the top pathway with p = 6.058e-06, hitting the same four metabolites. Six additional SMPDB disease pathways (Alkaptonuria, Tyrosinemia Type I, transient tyrosinemia, Hawkinsinuria, Dopamine beta-hydroxylase deficiency, and MAO-A deficiency) all share the identical four-compound hit set at FDR = 1.12e-09, establishing tyrosine catabolism disruption as the dominant biological signal. Metabolite ID reconciliation confirmed structural coherence across all five core tyrosine metabolites via matching InChIKey first-blocks, with no connectivity conflicts. Mummichog returned no hits (zero inputs resolved; input was KEGG IDs rather than m/z peaks), and FELLA failed at runtime, leaving the ORA results as the sole evidence base. Secondary PSEA hits included KEGG:hsa00400 (Phenylalanine, tyrosine and tryptophan biosynthesis, p=0.015) and KEGG:hsa00360 (Phenylalanine metabolism, p=0.0298), consistent with the metabolic proximity of phenylalanine and tyrosine pathways. Lysine metabolism (hsa00780, p=0.0372) and the urea cycle (hsa00220, p=0.0517) appear as weaker, single-metabolite signals. The biological story centres on a block in the L-tyrosine degradation cascade: L-tyrosine, 3,4-dihydroxyphenylacetaldehyde, norepinephrine, fumaric acid, and homogentisic acid are all differentially abundant, consistent with disruption of the aromatic amino acid catabolic arm shared by tyrosine, phenylalanine, and catecholamine biosynthesis pathways.

use run_ramp_enrichment (multi-DB ORA, broader namespace coverage) or run_metaboanalystr_psea (KEGG-specific ORA) instead

pathway_members.sqlite only indexes HUMAN1 + RECON2; for namespace 'KEGG', inspect the `metabolites_hit` list inside an EnrichmentResult (e.g. from run_ramp_enrichment) — it carries the method-specific compound roster
